I stopped writing UI boilerplate — this prompt gives me 90% of what I need.

5 min read
2 hours ago

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

I remember the exact moment I realized AI could handle my UI boilerplate. I was staring at a new feature spec, dreading the hours of typing interface Props, wiring up loading states, and writing the same responsive grid I'd written a hundred times before.
Then I asked an AI to do it for me.
The first result was generic. The second was better. By the fifth iteration, I had a prompt that consistently generates production-ready React components — complete with TypeScript, proper props, loading and error states, accessibility attributes, and even tests.
Here’s the exact prompt I use, why it works, and how you can adapt it for your stack.
The Problem: Vague Prompts Produce Generic Code
Most developers approach AI code generation wrong. They type something like “Create a user profile card component” and get back something that might work in a tutorial but falls apart in production.
The result is code that:

• Uses generic HTML instead of your component library

• Misses TypeScript types or uses…
